mission_priority: XRP intelligence and prediction-engine mastery; Barrot V3 remains execution and verification foundation.

confirmed_facts.claim: Circle Q2 2026 SEC filing reports USDC minted of USD83.004B and redeemed of USD86.784B in Q2, net USD-3.780B; H1 minted USD156.543B and redeemed USD158.540B, net USD-1.997B. Circle defines these as fiat converted to USDC and USDC converted to fiat, initiated by Circle Mint customers.

Circle Q2 2026 reported USD73.269B end-of-period USDC circulation, USD76.524B average circulation and a 3.5% reserve return rate. Its own 'USDC on platform' was USD12.442B at quarter end and 19.5% daily weighted-average share. Circle's platform definition includes Circle Mint accounts, corporate-held USDC and non-custodial wallets offered through Circle; this is not Coinbase's metric.

Circle's Q2 2026 filing reports USD324.6M Q2 and USD655.3M H1 distribution costs in connection with its Coinbase agreements. Coinbase's Q3 2026 10-Q says the Circle arrangement was renewed on the same terms. These costs are not Coinbase USDC balances or a direct measure of Coinbase's share of all USDC economics.

Coinbase's Q3 2026 deck reports USD22B average USDC held in Coinbase products, approximately 30% of USD73B average USDC market capitalization. The definition includes corporate USDC and customer USDC in eligible Coinbase products. Coinbase says the figure reflects a full-quarter impact of a Hyperliquid USDC balance that arrived in June. Its claim that it captured approximately 50% of USDC economics over the prior year is a company claim.

Coinbase Q3 2026 Form 10-Q reports USD8.616B USDC within September 30 Assets on Platform. AOP is a point-in-time customer asset measure and excludes assets for which customers hold full or partial keys. It is not the same population or time aggregation as the USD22B average product-balance metric.

Coinbase's September 30, 2026 collateral disclosures include USD1.2995B crypto assets held as collateral, USD389.657M crypto assets borrowed, USD1.976B loan receivables, USD3.284562B customer collateral not recognized as an asset or return obligation (USD2.804112B crypto and USD480.450M fiat/payment stablecoins), and USD301.943M recognized derivatives collateral. The derivatives table names BTC and ETH and states collateral requirements of at least 100% of derivative notional. No XRP-specific amount is disclosed; aggregate 'other crypto assets' is not an XRP balance.

Coinbase reports nine-month customer crypto collateral received of USD3.038805B and returned of USD2.731034B, and crypto loan receivables originated of USD3.562896B and repaid of USD3.562928B. These are gross aggregate flows, not XRP-specific flows. Coinbase says it does not use customer assets as collateral without customer consent.

Circle's September 17, 2026 SEC Form 8-K documents a five-year USDC promotion arrangement with Binance. Circle pays a monthly incentive based on USDC held through Circle's Modular Smart Contract Wallet infrastructure; Binance promotes USDC. Circle also issued Binance 1,237,011 Class A shares at USD80.84 for USD100M. Binance retains ordinary voting rights and accepted restrictions on transfer and hedging for up to two years, subject to exceptions. This does not establish control of Circle.

Circle and SBI Holdings each contributed approximately USD1.5M equivalent JPY to Circle SBI Japan K.K. in November 2025 and each own 50%. Circle consolidates the VIE because it controls the activities that most significantly affect the entity; SBI's interest is noncontrolling. Circle's Q2 filing says there were no significant operating results through June 30, 2026.

SBI Holdings and SBI Shinsei Bank each acquired USD25M of Circle shares at the June 2025 IPO, USD50M combined. SBI's historical approximately 9% Ripple shareholding is dated to the 2025 disclosure and is not a verified current cap table. SBI Group's current profile states 60% voting rights in SBI Ripple Asia as of March 31, 2026.

Circle announced Arc public mainnet on September 16, 2026. Circle says transaction fees are paid in USDC, the network has a permissioned validator set, Circle Payments Network and StableFX are integrated, and SBI Group is in the founding validator cohort. SBI said it intends to leverage USDC and JPYSC in the collaboration. Circle listed Coinbase and Binance among exchanges providing access to Arc, but the release does not establish the precise production scope of each exchange integration.

Circle USDC is natively issued on XRPL and supported through Circle Mint/APIs; Ripple's RLUSD is separately issued on XRPL and is distributed through Coinbase. Native USDC on XRPL does not by itself establish that XRP is used as a bridge asset in those transactions.

SBI Holdings and SMFG announced a capital/business alliance on October 30, 2026; SMFG's 5% participation is in SBI Startale Marketing. The announcement describes research and exploratory proof-of-concept work on JPYSC and stablecoin services, not a verified production service or XRP settlement route.

sourced_claims.claim: Coinbase says it captured approximately 50% of all USDC economics over the past year.

Circle says more than 100 institutional/ecosystem builders and more than 100 applications were part of the Arc launch ecosystem; the release also lists many entities as live on or exploring the private mainnet.
Circle lists Coinbase and Binance among digital-asset exchanges giving users/institutions access to Arc.

inferences: Circle is building a multi-rail USDC distribution strategy spanning Coinbase, Binance, SBI Japan and Arc, reducing dependence on any single distributor in principle; realized volume diversification is not yet measured.

SBI Group has documented strategic links to both Circle and Ripple, but these are separate equity investments, subsidiaries and joint ventures. The network overlap does not establish a unified control structure or coordinated XRP/USDC flows.

Arc's USDC-denominated gas and institutional validator model may compete with XRPL/Ripple for some stablecoin settlement use cases, while Circle's native USDC deployment on XRPL shows a multi-chain coexistence strategy.

Coinbase's USD22B average product USDC and USD8.616B September 30 USDC AOP are not contradictory figures; they differ by definition, customer/corporate scope and average-versus-point-in-time measurement.
Coinbase's aggregate collateral disclosures demonstrate institutional collateral activity at scale but do not establish XRP collateral demand or asset-level XRP exposure.
speculation: Arc could capture some future stablecoin payment and FX flows that might otherwise use XRPL or other payment rails. No comparative production-volume evidence establishes displacement.
SBI's investments and validator roles could make it an important distribution and infrastructure hub across Circle and Ripple ecosystems; the extent of actual commercial coordination remains unknown.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Circle is diversifying USDC distribution across Coinbase, Binance, SBI and Arc, reducing concentration in any one channel.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: Coinbase's Q3 deck claims approximately 50% of USDC economics; Circle's Q2 Coinbase distribution costs were USD655.3M in H1. No current partner-level USDC volume split is available.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Arc may compete with XRPL for institutional stablecoin settlement while coexisting through Circle's multi-chain USDC strategy.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: Circle supports native USDC on XRPL; no matched Arc-versus-XRPL payment, FX, liquidity or active-wallet data are available.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Coinbase's USD22B average USDC product balance and USD8.616B period-end USDC AOP measure different populations and time aggregation.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: No single reconciliation schedule bridges every balance in the average-products measure to the AOP table; the definitions nevertheless explicitly differ.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Coinbase's aggregate collateral and derivatives infrastructure could create indirect XRP financing or liquidity links.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: The filing names BTC and ETH in recognized derivatives collateral; 'other crypto assets' is aggregated and no XRP amount or XRP-specific product is disclosed.

market_observations.definition: Average product balance includes corporate USDC and customer USDC in eligible Coinbase products; AOP is period-end customer assets and excludes assets where customers hold full or partial keys.

unknowns_or_limitations: Circle Q3 2026 results were scheduled for November 4, 2026; Q3 USDC circulation, mint/redemption and reserve-yield figures were not available at this cutoff.
Coinbase's Q3 collateral disclosures do not identify an XRP-specific amount. The aggregate 'other crypto assets' category prevents asserting either zero XRP exposure or a positive XRP balance.
Coinbase's USD22B average product metric and USD8.616B period-end AOP do not have a published line-by-line reconciliation.
Circle's post-June 30, 2026 Circle SBI Japan JV operating results and actual USDC distribution volumes in Japan remain unknown.
Arc public-mainnet transaction volume, active institutional settlement, actual Coinbase/Binance production integration scope and JPYSC live use are not established by the launch release.
SBI Holdings' approximately 9% Ripple stake is historical 2025 evidence; a current October 2026 cap table is unavailable.
Circle Mint mint/redemption figures are customer-initiated primary-market fiat conversions, not all USDC transfers, secondary-market trades or all stablecoin capital flows.
No causal XRP demand, price effect or market-share displacement has been measured from Circle, Coinbase, Binance, SBI or Arc relationships.
